10.1016/j.jag.2026.105373.abstract: Satellite-based solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) provides a useful proxy for photosynthetic activity, but satellite retrieval remains challenging because the fluorescence signal is weak relative to top-of-atmosphere radiance and is further affected by atmospheric and surface scattering. Existing GOME-2 retrievals have largely relied on mechanistic linear decomposition methods, such as singular value decomposition (SVD)-based approaches, whereas more recent machine-learning methods often depend on pre-existing SIF products for training or post-processing. Here, we develop a simulation-trained neural-network framework, termed NN-SIF, for retrieving far-red SIF (740 nm) directly from GOME-2 radiance. The model is trained exclusively on synthetic spectra generated from coupled SCOPE and MODTRAN simulations, with explicit representation of mixed-pixel conditions, observation geometry, and atmospheric variability. Independent synthetic validation shows that NN-SIF outperforms both SVD-SIF and noise-reduced SIF (NR-SIF), reducing RMSE by up to 70% and achieving an R2 of 0.91. Applied to GOME-2 observations, NN-SIF reproduces large-scale seasonal and spatial SIF patterns broadly consistent with the benchmark NR-SIF product. Additional comparison with TROPOMI SIF further supports the large-scale consistency of the retrieval, while also highlighting structured regional discrepancies that warrant cautious interpretation. Cross-platform consistency between Metop-B and Metop-C suggests that the trained framework can be transferred across GOME-2 sensors without sensor-specific retraining. Overall, this study shows that physically informed synthetic training data can support a viable nonlinear retrieval pathway for coarse-resolution SIF observations. Rather than replacing existing methods, NN-SIF extends the current set of retrieval strategies available for large-scale fluorescence monitoring.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105373.title: Global retrieval of GOME-2 sun-induced chlorophyll fluorescence via neural networks trained on mixed-pixel simulations
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105373.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105385.abstract: Intra-annual double disturbances (sequential disturbances occurring within a single year, such as slash-and-burn) in tropical regions result in more significant ecosystem impacts than single disturbances. However, optical data-based monitoring is limited by insufficient continuous spatio-temporal observations. Approaches using higher-frequency Sentinel-1 (S1) data, relying solely on temporal or spatial features, struggle to distinguish double disturbances due to noise and temporal heterogeneity. To address this issue, we propose an approach that employs a three-dimensional deep learning architecture to simultaneously extract multi-level embedded spatial context and temporal change characteristics—such as magnitude and duration features from time series S1 data to differentiate single and double disturbances. Additionally, we tested the effectiveness of incorporating an attention mechanism into the model to highlight key spatio-temporal features and suppress irrelevant information. The optimal model was applied to map double disturbances in three deforestation hotspot states in the Brazilian Amazon for 2019, identifying the first disturbance time at a monthly scale and verifying slash-and-burn by overlaying burned area maps. Results show that (1) the 3D U-Net model effectively extracted the spatio-temporal information of doubles disturbance in S1 data (F1 score of 0.912), and the integration of the attention mechanism highlighted distinctive temporal features, improving the balanced accuracy by 2.7%; (2) The optimal model (i.e., 3D U-Net with attention mechanism) exhibited potential generalization capability when mapping double disturbances in three states for 2019, with user’s accuracy and producer’s accuracy exceeding 0.85, and the estimated double disturbances area in three states in 2019 were 2685 ± 189 km2; (3) 53.57% of mapped forest disturbances were double disturbances, 94.4% of which occurred outside the protected areas, highlighting the critical role of protected areas in ecological preservation. This study presents a novel S1-based framework for accurately characterizing intra-annual slash-and-burn events on a finer-grained spatial and temporal scale, providing useful information for carbon emission estimation and the development of effective conservation interventions.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105385.title: Mapping slash-and-burn in humid tropical rainforests based on Sentinel-1 imagery and 3D deep learning
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105385.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105377.abstract: Accurate mangrove mapping faces persistent challenges from spectral confusion and tidal fluctuations. This study develops a robust classification framework that strategically integrates geographical knowledge with deep learning architectures specifically designed for multi-modal data fusion. We incorporate spatialtemporal texture patterns and tide-resilient phenological features alongside spectral and SAR data. A multi-branch network architecture with dedicated processing streams preserves modality-specific characteristics while attention mechanisms enable adaptive feature weighting and fusion. Evaluated across three Chinese coastal sites, our method achieved superior overall accuracies (95.14%, 94.21%, and 96.66%), outperforming benchmarks by 0.78–8.60%. The framework demonstrated exceptional mangrove identification capability and maintained robust performance with limited samples. This work validates that combining domain-specific feature engineering with specialized deep learning structures for multi-modal fusion creates an effective solution for coastal wetland monitoring, offering both high accuracy and practical utility for conservation applications.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105377.title: Overcoming spectral and tidal challenges in mangrove mapping with a multi-modal deep learning network fusing phenological and texture features
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105377.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105386.abstract: Long-term monitoring of aboveground biomass (AGB) is essential for assessing ecosystem productivity and carbon storage. However, sparse vegetation and complex bare-soil backgrounds in desert regions introduce significant uncertainties in AGB inversion and driver analysis. In this study, field plots, UAVs, and satellite data were integrated to develop high-accuracy AGB inversion models for desert ecosystems using vegetation classification, data fusion, and multi-model comparison. Theil–Sen slope estimation, Mann–Kendall tests, and SHAP analysis were applied to characterize AGB dynamics and identify the driving mechanisms. The results show that object-based classification combined with deep learning (SegFormer) achieved the highest accuracy (OA = 94%). Vegetation-class-based variables improved UAV-scale AGB estimation. At the satellite-scale, spectral features generated by Landsat–MODIS fusion, combined with environmental variables, yielded the best performance with the Boruta–XGBoost model (R2 = 0.84 RMSE = 733.32 kg ha⁻1, CCC = 0.91). From 2000 to 2024, AGB exhibited an increasing trend, with 57.6% of the area increasing mainly in low-elevation temperate desert regions, while 37.9% decreased primarily in high-elevation temperate desert steppe regions. Temperature and precipitation were the dominant drivers of AGB variation, with notable interaction effects involving temperature-precipitation and potential evapotranspiration-precipitation. When precipitation exceeded 82 mm, the effects of temperature and potential evapotranspiration on AGB were enhanced and became positive influences. This study provides methodological support for AGB modeling and informs desertification management in arid regions.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105386.title: Machine-learning framework for cross-scale estimation of desert vegetation aboveground biomass and driver analysis in the Junggar Basin using UAV classification and satellite data fusion
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105386.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105381.abstract: Individual tree segmentation (ITS) is of great importance for forest resource surveys. Point cloud-based ITS, which uses deep learning methods, has become a research hotspot. However, the state-of-the-art reported works struggle to accurately segment individual trees in scenarios characterized by canopy overlap and low-density point clouds. To address these limitations, we proposed a Dual-branch Bounding Box-Embedding Network (DBE-Net), which adopts the bounding box branch to delimit the spatial extents of individual trees, thereby providing initial segmentation constraints. Subsequently, foreground points and background points are segmented within these bounding boxes to generate candidate results. The core novelty of DBE-Net lies in its dual-branch architecture that fuses proposal-based and clustering-based instance segmentation paradigms, which effectively alleviates the reliance on a single prediction branch and improves both accuracy and efficiency. The bounding box branch yields higher-quality candidate results than the offset vector branch, eliminates the need for a time-consuming clustering process, and enhances the recognition accuracy of adjacent trees. We selected ForAINet, TreeLearn, TD3D, and other representative models as baselines to conduct comparative experiments. The results show that DBE-Net exhibited superior segmentation performance, achieving 84.9% F1-score, 90.5% precision, 81.0% recall, and 73.5% coverage. In terms of predicting candidate results, the bounding box branch is 3.2 times faster than the offset vector branch. Moreover, extensive experiments and visualizations further exhibit the robustness and adaptability of DBE-Net, whose F1-score variation is within 3% under different hyperparameter settings. This study demonstrates that DBE-Net can achieve accurate and efficient individual tree segmentation, thereby providing a solid foundation for subsequent forest surveys. The code can be found at https://github.com/liangwenge740/DBE-Net.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105381.title: DBE-Net: a dual-branch bounding box-embedding network for individual tree segmentation from LiDAR
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105381.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105375.abstract: A major gap in long-term, large-scale land surface monitoring is the absence of consistent Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS)-like data prior to its 2000 launch. A few data fusion methods have attempted to model pre-2000 MODIS-like data, yet they struggle to balance trade-offs among temporal extent, spatial coverage, and spatial continuity. We propose a novel Target self-Attention Spatiotemporal Fusion (TASTF) model that bridges the scale gap between Landsat (30 m) and Global Inventory Modeling and Mapping Studies (GIMMS) (∼8 km) data to generate seamless, 500-m biweekly MODIS-like Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) data dating back to 1984 over the contiguous United States (CONUS). The model integrates a robust optimal image mosaicking method to construct spatially extensive Landsat reference data across CONUS. To enhance spatial continuity, we develop a target self-attention mechanism that embeds patch-wise day-of-year data into the self-attention module to dynamically prioritize target-region pixels, effectively suppressing patch artifacts. Experimental results demonstrate that the TASTF effectively simulates MODIS-like data with accurate spatial details and temporal variations. Post-2000 reconstructions show strong agreement with real MODIS observations, achieving a regional annual root mean square error of 0.089, substantially outperforming GIMMS dataset (0.154). Compared with advanced deep learning models, TASTF results exhibit superior spatial continuity and temporal consistency, achieving a correlation coefficient of 0.993, higher than those of comparison models (0.983 and 0.981). The proposed model and generated MODIS-like data contribute valuable support for long-term, fine-scale land surface monitoring and analysis.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105375.title: Reconstructing 500-m NDVI time series since 1984 using a target self-attention spatiotemporal fusion model
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105375.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105409.abstract: Speckle contamination strongly affects the interpretability and practical application of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery. For real dual-polarization SAR data, despeckling is particularly difficult because clean supervision is unavailable and temporal variations between acquisitions complicate the characterization of speckle behavior. Existing unsupervised deep models have shown promise, but many of them still underuse the complementary information contained in neighboring temporal observations and insufficiently exploit the physical cues associated with polarimetric scattering, which may result in structural degradation and distortion of scattering characteristics. To address these limitations, we develop CD2P-Net, a collaborative dual-domain progressive network for real dual-polarization SAR despeckling. The method is established within a physically guided multitemporal unsupervised learning framework, where spatial, spectral, and temporal relationships are progressively modeled to make better use of temporal coherence and speckle variability across adjacent acquisitions. In addition, covariance-derived statistics and polarimetric decomposition descriptors are introduced to improve the physical reliability of the learned features. Experiments on real Sentinel-1 dual-polarization time-series data show that the proposed method achieves superior despeckling performance compared with representative competing approaches, while better preserving spatial structures, polarimetric characteristics, and semantic consistency.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105409.title: Physically consistent multitemporal dual-domain learning for dual-polarization SAR despeckling
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105409.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105392.abstract: NASA’s EMIT hyperspectral spectrometer provides high spectral (∼7.4 nm) and spatial (60 m) resolution, capabilities that have not been routinely applied to water quality monitoring in shallow aquatic systems, where the bio-optical properties are highly complex. In this study, we developed Hyper-MoE-VAE, a deep-learning inversion framework integrating a mixture-of-experts architecture with variational autoencoders for globally applicable hyperspectral water-quality retrievals. The model accommodates diverse water types and addresses one-to-many inversions to retrieve chlorophyll-a (Chl a) and phytoplankton absorption coefficient (aphy) from hyperspectral remote sensing reflectance (Rrs). Hyper-MoE-VAE was trained on a global bio-optical dataset and applied to EMIT imagery over Lake Pontchartrain. Same-day field matchups acquired on 14 April 2025 provide the first validation of EMIT-derived Chl a (MAPE = 7.66 %; MAE = 1.13 in log10 space, unitless) and aphy across all EMIT bands, with representative performance (NRMSE = 0.09–0.11 m−1; ε = 29–36 %), revealing a muted Chl a response under highly turbid freshwater conditions and a clear shift toward chlorophyte dominance following fresh inputs. In addition, PACE-OCI, also hyperspectral with lower spatial resolution, was compared with EMIT for Chl a retrievals. Both sensors show comparable spatial patterns despite differences in spectral and spatial resolution, supporting the Hyper-MoE-VAE’s cross-mission applicability. These findings demonstrate EMIT’s strong potential for characterizing phytoplankton dynamics, both in abundance and community composition, and for monitoring harmful algal blooms (HABs) in aquatic systems.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105392.title: NASA’s EMIT hyperspectral observations of phytoplankton ecology in estuarine waters
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105392.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105367.abstract: Wheat is a major global staple, and accurate yield estimation is critical for agricultural management and food security. While satellite and UAV-based approaches are widely used, they are costly and operationally complex, making ground-based RGB imagery an attractive low-cost alternative. However, existing image-based methods are often limited by the restricted representational power of handcrafted features or the limited interpretability of end-to-end deep learning models. This study therefore develops a ground-based RGB framework to systematically evaluate the roles of explicit handcrafted features and deep implicit features in wheat yield estimation. Explicit features describe spike morphology and canopy color using spatial geometry, wavelet-based texture, and visible vegetation indices, while implicit features are extracted from a VGG-based segmentation encoder. Four regression models (RF, SVM, KNN, and XGBoost) were tested. The results show that both feature types are informative, but implicit features provide superior predictive performance. In particular, XGBoost with implicit features achieved the highest accuracy (R2 = 0.85, RMSE = 1015.77 kg·ha⁻1, rRMSE = 12.9%), outperforming models based only on explicit features and matching the performance of combined feature sets. Overall, the proposed approach clarifies the relative roles of different feature representations and provides a flexible and practical solution for low-cost, scalable crop yield assessment based on ground-based RGB imagery.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105367.title: A flexible framework for wheat yield estimation from ground-based RGB imagery: evaluating explicit and implicit feature representations
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105367.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105387.abstract: UAV remote sensing demands efficient, large-scale mapping for critical applications such as emergency response and resource surveying. However, traditional single-agent SLAM is inherently constrained by limited flight endurance, rendering the transition to multi-UAV collaborative frameworks imperative. We propose MSRS-SLAM, a novel real-time dense reconstruction framework for UAV swarms. The pipeline utilizes visual odometry for pose estimation, followed by deep multi-view depth estimation to generate local dense maps. To resolve multi-agent consistency challenges, we introduce a robust two-stage map fusion strategy : the first stage achieves initial alignment through 3D-3D feature matching by leveraging multi-frame co-visibility, RANSAC, and the Umeyama algorithm, while the second stage employs dense point cloud registration for precise relative pose refinement. Global consistency is ensured by eliminating accumulated errors through intra-agent and inter-agent loop closure detection coupled with global Pose Graph Optimization. Furthermore, an improved SAM3 model based on text prompts is integrated, enabling multi-UAV cooperative semantic dense reconstruction. Evaluation on four real-world datasets demonstrates that MSRS-SLAM achieves high localization accuracy with an Absolute Pose Error (APE) ranging from 0.21 m to 0.70 m. In terms of efficiency, the system maintains a stable processing throughput, completing the reconstruction of 495 images within 6.34 min for the Village dataset, representing a several-fold reduction in average processing time relative to offline baselines. These results indicate that MSRS-SLAM attains an optimal balance between computational efficiency and reconstruction precision, significantly enhancing the viability of real-time collaborative mapping.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105387.title: MSRS-SLAM: A real-time multi-UAV dense mapping system for efficient low-altitude remote sensing
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105387.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105436.abstract: Air-pollution exposure is a growing public-health and urban-governance concern in Africa, but comparable subnational evidence remains limited. This study constructs an Africa-wide Administrative Level 1 (ADM1) panel for 2019–2023 using Sentinel-5P TROPOMI tropospheric nitrogen dioxide (NO2), LandScan population, settlement, meteorological, and topographic data. We estimate area-mean NO2 and population-weighted NO2 exposure, quantify within-country inequality, assess population-pollution alignment, and examine interpretable natural and human-related associations. Population-weighted NO2 exposure is spatially persistent and highly uneven, with elevated burdens concentrated in North African coastal and Nile-corridor regions, Southern African urban-industrial zones, and selected metropolitan or industrial ADM1 units elsewhere. Continental mean exposure declined slightly in 2020 and rebounded above the 2019 level from 2021 onward, consistent with a short-lived disruption of traffic and industrial activity during the COVID-19 period. National averages concealed strong internal concentration, with a limited number of ADM1 units carrying disproportionate national burden. Random held-out validation indicated strong predictive structure, while country-blocked validation exposed limited out-of-country transferability. Interpretable machine-learning attribution using XGBoost and SHAP showed that nighttime lights and built-environment indicators were strongly associated with exposure, while wind, temperature, precipitation, elevation, and slope further shaped the observed patterns. Sensitivity analyses showed that ADM1-level exposure rankings were robust to NO2-to-population-grid alignment choices and that GHSL built-environment covariates were stable between 2020 and 2025; independent near-surface NO2 evidence in Accra further showed moderate spatial agreement and consistent Harmattan enhancement with satellite-derived NO2. The framework provides an Earth-observation-based baseline for identifying priority subnational regions, tracking exposure inequality, and supporting SDG 3- and SDG 11-relevant air-quality governance in data-scarce African settings.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105436.title: Satellite-derived population-weighted NO2 exposure and inequality across African subnational regions for SDGs 3 and 11
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105436.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105395.abstract: High-precision soil quality monitoring is vital for precision agriculture. Recently, swarm intelligence (SI) algorithms have become essential for identifying hyperspectral features. Aiming at the challenges of high dimensionality in soil fertility indicator retrieval, this paper integrates ZY1-02E satellite and HyMap airborne data to conduct feature selection and fertility estimation using an improved slime mould algorithm (ISMA). ISMA integrates three synergistic stages: (1) spectrally-informed initialization and pre-screening for redundancy reduction, (2) a multi-level location update strategy for balancing exploration and exploitation, and (3) a complementary stagnation control strategy for late stage search refinement. A customized fitness function is designed to optimize the estimation of soil fertility indicators. The effectiveness of the proposed ISMA was first validated on ZY1-02E satellite imagery. Experimental results demonstrated that the ISMA-XGBoost model yielded the best optimization capability, achieving the test R2 of 0.752 for soil organic matter (SOM) on ZY1-02E data, and its multi-indicator applicability was confirmed with R2 values of 0.675 (total phosphorus), 0.670 (total potassium), and 0.678 (total nitrogen). The model’s reliability was validated on independent HyMap data (R2 = 0.757), a significant improvement over conventional algorithm (R2 = 0.730). These findings provide critical technical support for regional precision agriculture.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105395.title: An improved slime mould algorithm applied to hyperspectral feature selection in soil fertility indicators
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105395.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105454.abstract: Terraces are a defining feature of Mediterranean mountain landscapes, enabling agriculture on steep slopes while providing multiple ecosystem services. Land suitability analysis (LSA) can guide authorities and land users to sustainably manage and expand these environments. It typically requires fully labelled datasets, but in many real-world applications only a fraction of positive examples is available, with the rest unlabelled. This study aims to present an integrated predictive modelling framework that combines GIS with data-driven Machine Learning (ML) techniques, capable of learning from Positive and Unlabelled (PU) datasets for LSA. The proposed framework was applied to develop a terrace suitability map for Cyprus’ Troodos Mountains. A 5-m DEM was processed to extract the mountain area, with elevation ≥ 500 m and slopes ≥ 15%, defining the study area. Crop plots registered under the Single Area Payment Scheme of the European Common Agricultural Policy were used to classify the study area into Terrace-Present (TP) and Terrace-Absent (TA) cells, with TP serving as labelled positive and TA as unlabelled samples. A two-step ML approach was applied, first identifying reliable negatives from TA cells, then using these with TP cells for suitability prediction. The developed PU-classifier was evaluated under the selected completely-at-random (SCAR) assumption, achieving a Recall of 84.6%, Precision of 81.5% and an F1 score of 83%. Feature importance analysis identified land cover, terrain slope and tree cover density as the most influential parameters for terrace suitability. Comparative analysis between 2017 and 2024 revealed abandonment of terraced agricultural land (29% decrease) as well as revitalisation (12% increase). The resulting suitability map and accompanying data layers are accessible through a Google Earth Engine application, aiming to support informed decision-making for sustainable landscape planning.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105454.title: A machine learning framework for predicting agricultural terrace suitability using positive and unlabelled datasets: an application for the Troodos Mountains, Cyprus
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105454.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105434.abstract: Facilitated by the BIOMASS mission, P-band polarimetric SAR interferometry (PolInSAR) provides a key capability for large-scale forest height mapping and biomass estimation. Within this context, the random volume over ground (RVoG) model stands out for its physical consistency and broad applicability. However, at P-band, deviations of canopy backscattering from the exponential extinction assumption in RVoG lead to biased height estimates. While gaussian vertical backscatter (GVB) offers greater flexibility, its surplus parameters and unconstrained convergence raise robustness concerns, resulting in estimation biases that limit its widespread application. To address these challenges, a convolutional neural network (CNN) is used to link structure parameters to SAR observations, thereby imposing prior constraints. A parameter-guided GVB (PG-GVB) variant is developed within a three-stage framework, achieving improved performance while explicitly analyzing how different parameters influence robustness. Validation on BioSAR-2008 and AfriSAR-2016 shows that the best-constrained configuration reduces forest height errors by 20.5% (4.83 m to 3.84 m) and 26.5% (7.49 m to 5.50 m) relative to the exponential model at Krycklan and Lopé, respectively. These results reveal transferable optimization strategies, with shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis further quantifying feature contributions.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105434.title: PG-GVB: A prior constrained backscatter framework for P-band PolInSAR forest height inversion
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105434.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105464.abstract: Accurate large-scale mapping of coastal dune types is critical for coastal management but remains challenging due to the dunes’ high spatial heterogeneity and the spectral complexity in coastal environments. Therefore, this study aims to develop a coastal dune mapping approach and demonstrate its applicability across Australia and New Zealand. Firstly, we leveraged geological maps to delineate the spatial extent of coastal dune fields, effectively masking out non-dune areas. Secondly, we applied an object-based image analysis (OBIA), followed by a random forest classifier that integrated multi-source features to classify six coastal dune types within the delineated coastal dune fields, including active dunes, foredunes, sandy beaches, semi-stabilized dunes, stabilized dunes, and wetlands (dune slacks). Based on this approach, we generated a 10 m fine classification map of coastal dune types across Australia and New Zealand, covering a total area of 27,564 km2. Accuracy assessment yielded an overall classification accuracy of 90.68 %. Most categories achieved satisfactory performance, with stabilized dunes showing the highest accuracy (96.81 %). We also found that approximately 498 km2 of coastal dune area has been converted to urban development land. However, this development pressure was mitigated by conservation efforts, as 15,781.80 km2 (59.44 %) of the total coastal dune area was situated within protected areas. This study provides a replicable methodology for large-scale fine classification of coastal dune types. The resulting map offers scientific support for monitoring coastal dune systems state and evolution under human intervention.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105464.title: Mapping the extent, type and remnant areas of the coastal dunes of Australia and New Zealand by integrating multi-source data
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105464.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105465.abstract: Bathymetric inversion in turbid tidal channels remains challenging because of degraded bottom-related optical signals and complex-branched channel networks. This study investigates whether geomorphic structure can act as a stable prior for bathymetric reconstruction when the spectral-depth relationship breaks down. We develop a geomorphology-constrained framework that integrates UAV multispectral imagery, suspended sediment concentration, RTK-derived channel depths, and adjacent flat DEM constraints. A branching centerline network is first extracted to characterize channel organization, from which geometric and network-structural predictors, including normalized width, width-to-depth ratio, downstream accumulation, tributary order, and distance to junctions, are derived and used to construct a random-forest depth prior. Then, these predictors are refined through constrained optimization with anisotropic smoothing along channel directions and boundary consistency with exposed terrain. The framework is tested in a turbid tidal-channel system along the southern Yellow Sea and further evaluated through a transfer experiment in the Yangtze Estuary. Among all predictors, the width-to-depth ratio provides the greatest improvement in inversion accuracy, reducing RMSE from 0.30 m to 0.18 m (38 %), highlighting the dominantly geomorphological control on channel cross-sectional geometry. Overall, The provided framework achieves RMSE values of 0.15 m (RTK-based) and 0.23 m (DEM-based), outperforming empirical spectral, conventional machine-learning, and deep-learning approaches, particularly in scour zones, narrow tributaries, and channel confluences. In the Yangtze Estuary, the model attains an RMSE of 3.46 m (R2 = 0.70), suggesting preliminary transferability across more than three orders (from ∼ 10 m to 10 km) of magnitude in channel scale. The results show that the main bottleneck in turbid tidal-channel inversion is not only optical degradation, but also the lack of geomorphic organization in model design. By coupling data-driven learning with structural and boundary constraints, this study advances a transferable inversion paradigm for optically complex coastal environments.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105465.title: Geomorphology-constrained bathymetric inversion of turbid tidal channels using centerline-network priors and machine learning
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105465.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105471.abstract: Mapping unregulated solid waste dumps from remote sensing imagery is important for environmental risk assessment and sustainable development monitoring, but remains constrained by the high cost of pixel-level annotation. Weakly supervised semantic segmentation (WSSS) with image-level labels reduces annotation effort, yet often suffers from incomplete object activation, especially for waste dumps with irregular morphology, variable object scales, and visually confusing backgrounds. To address this problem, we propose a label-efficient mixed-supervision framework that uses image-level labels as semantic regularization and a small fraction of pixel-level masks as spatial anchors. The framework adopts an asymmetric design: the semantic learning stream regularizes backbone representations during training, while the spatial grounding stream learns the final segmentation path. During inference, the auxiliary semantic stream is removed, enabling direct segmentation without CAM-to-pseudo-label refinement or separate segmentation-network retraining. Within the semantic learning stream, the proposed SAM-FMR module combines an adopted Slice-and-Merge (SAM) strategy with Feature Masked Recovery (FMR). SAM preserves local details through slice-level processing, whereas FMR applies structured masking in the high-level feature space to encourage context-aware feature learning and more spatially distributed semantic responses. The framework further provides modular interfaces for interchangeable CAM-based weak-supervision modules and backbone-adaptive segmentation heads. Experiments on the newly constructed YREB dataset and the enhanced Global Dumpsite benchmark show that the proposed method improves over few-shot, pure weakly supervised, and semi-supervised label-efficient baselines under spatially independent validation, cross-dataset transfer, and conventional patch-level benchmarks. With only 1% pixel-level annotations, it reaches nearly 90% of the same-framework fully supervised reference, demonstrating a favorable trade-off between dense-annotation cost and segmentation performance. The datasets and source code are publicly available.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105471.title: Label-efficient mapping of unregulated waste dumps via mixed supervision with feature masked recovery
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105471.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105462.abstract: Monitoring shallow-water marine ecosystems requires precise, low-cost and reproducible methods, yet traditional diver-based surveys are labor-intensive, subject to observer bias and limited in spatial coverage. In this study, we present an autonomous framework that integrates deep learning techniques with open-source data acquisition platforms to overcome these challenges. Our approach uses a transformer-based model to classify different coral morphotypes, seagrass species and benthic habitats. This model is trained on the publicly available Seatizen Atlas image dataset. Data were collected using low-cost autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs) equipped with action cameras, differential GNSS receivers, single-beam echosounders and inertial measurement units. The ASVs provide precise geolocation, depth and attitude measurements, synchronized with image timestamps and embedded as standardized metadata, ensuring interoperability and reproducibility. Beyond image classification, the ASVs enable bathymetric surveys and photogrammetric reconstruction for three-dimensional mapping of surveyed areas. Field validation at Réunion Island and Aldabra Atoll demonstrates that this framework delivers cost-effective, non-invasive and standardized monitoring, while automating laborious annotation tasks and increasing survey scalability. By combining open-source datasets, AI models and versatile ASV functionalities, this methodology supports reproducible ecological assessments and informs conservation decisions.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105462.title: Reproducible mapping of marine biodiversity using autonomous surface vehicles and deep learning
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105462.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105473.abstract: High-resolution UAV observations provide a novel perspective for monitoring wildfire dynamics. This study explores a new approach for wildfire prediction by integrating high-precision, multi-source spatial data. We introduce 3DConv-U-Net, a deep learning model designed to capture spatiotemporal spread patterns. The architecture uses a 3D convolutional backbone to process continuous fire sequences and a separate encoder for environmental factors. To address the scarcity of real-world data, we developed a simulation pipeline to generate minute-level synthetic dataset. This allows the model to learn the physical rules of fire spread at a high temporal resolution. Experimental results show that the model generalizes effectively from 30 m simulation data to 1 m UAV observations. Our approach achieves higher performance with a Sorensen index of 0.959 and a Jaccard index of 0.921. Notably, the model demonstrates improvements in computational complexity and inference for lightweight optimization. Compared to the Transformer-based model, it reduces the parameter count by 70% and achieves an efficient inference time of 47.8 ms/batch, providing a practical tool for real-time edge computing. This work demonstrates that data-driven models can maintain spatial consistency across different scales. The results can support continuous wildfire monitoring and more reliable emergency decision-making.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105473.title: Integrating UAV image time-series with multi-source environmental features for sequential wildfire spread prediction
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105473.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105483.abstract: High spectral resolution of hyperspectral sensors facilitates the detailed identification of material, but the coarse spatial resolution affects accurate interpretation. In this regard, spectral unmixing techniques attempt to estimate the constituent materials (endmembers) and their fractional areas (abundances) within a pixel’s instantaneous field of view (IFOV). However, many existing methods optimize denoising, endmember detection, and abundance estimation separately, which can limit robustness under noise and spectral variability. The current study proposes a self-supervised deep learning framework for joint hyperspectral unmixing and denoising. A noise-aware probabilistic encoding strategy is adopted to model a structured latent space to implicitly detect the endmembers. Further, the proposed encoding scheme and regularizations ensure spatio-spectral fidelity to improve robustness to noise. Additionally, a contrastive learning mechanism is incorporated to improve latent separability and robustness to spectral variability. The framework also integrates available partial endmember priors when present and employs a policy-based adaptive refinement mechanism to update endmember estimates under complex noise and mixing conditions. In addition, a learnable loss-balancing strategy is introduced to reduce manual tuning and stabilize optimization. Experiments on synthetic and real hyperspectral datasets demonstrate strong and balanced performance across reconstruction accuracy, spectral fidelity, and clustering quality, indicating the effectiveness of the proposed framework for practical hyperspectral unmixing.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105483.title: Self-supervised spectral unmixing using scene-aware deep priors
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105483.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105489.abstract: Large-scale maize mapping is challenging due to the lack of field-level datasets, which were essential for training machine learning models. The United States (US) provides abundant in-situ labels and national maize maps while Argentina and Brazil offered limited data and double-cropping further complicates mapping. In this study, we propose a survey-free method for maize mapping in Argentina and Brazil, with cropping intensity considered. We first pre-trained a maize classifier on US cornfields using Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) Relative Height (RH) metrics and Sentinel-2 imagery, then transferred this model to Argentina and Brazil to produce candidate maize labels at peak growth. We distinguished maize from other crops using phenology-based empirical thresholds. These high-confidence labels were then used to train a Random Forest model. Finally, we validated the maps with Google Street View (GSV) imagery and benchmark maps. Our framework produced 18,481 maize and 15,725 non-maize labels in Argentina and 2,125 first-season maize, 7,406 s-season maize and 7,643 non-maize in Brazil. Evaluation of our maize maps against GSV images showed satisfactory agreement, with accuracies around 90 %. The maps also aligned well with benchmark maps, exhibiting 91 % accuracy for Argentina and 88 % for Brazil. Our proposed frameworks can enhance maize mapping where field surveys are challenging.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105489.title: Enabling maize mapping in double-cropping regions of Argentina and Brazil without ground reference data by leveraging multiple satellite platforms
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105489.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105469.abstract: Matter-loaded windrows are high-density submesoscale accumulation structures that form on the ocean surface and are often associated with extreme environmental events. This study presents a framework for windrow detection using a UNet deep-learning model applied to Planet SuperDove (PSD) 8-band satellite imagery (FLODAS). The model is trained on hand-annotated cases representing a variety of windrows and evaluated using complementary performance metrics, demonstrating consistent detection across independent scenes, while also revealing scene-specific patterns of false positives. Spectral analysis and classification based on the spectral angle distance metric is used to examine the potential for discriminating floating matter types using the PSD bands. Limited ground-truth data and the incomplete spectral characterisation of floating matter currently constrain classification performance. Application of the framework in the Aegean Sea enabled the identification of surface matter accumulations linked to storm-driven runoff and riverine discharge. The results demonstrate the potential of the framework to support in situ sampling and debris-removal operations, as well as short-term assessments of matter transport and windrow dynamics. Overall, the proposed framework represents a proof-of-concept step towards the development of operational detection systems for surface matter and marine debris accumulations.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105469.title: SuperDove satellite detection of matter-loaded windrows with a focus on extreme environmental events
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105469.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105497.abstract: Precise characterization of alfalfa growth dynamics is essential for breeding accessions with superior regrowth capacity, persistence, and yield stability. However, traditional plot level and coarse scale observations suffer from low signal to noise ratios particularly before canopy closure when phenotypic data are strongly affected by weeds and soil background. Moreover, existing studies rarely capture the dynamic mechanisms of crop development across the entire growth cycle. To address this, the DINO-Pheno-Cluster framework is introduced as a foundation model driven and mechanism decomposed phenotyping approach. This decoupled framework first utilizes DINO-XMem, a few-shot individual plant segmentation network based on DINOv3 and a dual memory mechanism. It subsequently applies parameterized dynamic modeling guided by growth process knowledge. Validation utilized high frequency Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery from 12 time points across three growing seasons covering 127 alfalfa accessions. DINO-XMem achieved an 89.54% mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) under a 10-shot setting and maintained 86.77% under extreme 1-shot conditions. It successfully resolved dense canopy oversegmentation outperforming fully supervised baselines by 4.08% to 11.97% in mIoU. Crucially, the extracted high purity time series trajectories were parameterized into specific biological indicators including maximum growth rate, comprehensive regeneration index, and seasonal stability index. Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) clustering based on these mechanistic traits identified four distinct functional ideotypes comprising High yield/High regrowth, Upright/Sparse, High stability/Persistent, and Short/Dense, all validated by ground measured biomass. This workflow establishes a precision screening tool for multi harvest crops advancing crop phenomics toward process level analysis.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105497.title: DINO-Pheno-Cluster: Integrating few-shot foundation models and UAV time-series for spatiotemporal growth and functional characterization of alfalfa
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105497.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105493.abstract: Accurate global sea surface wind speed retrieval under high-wind conditions (> 15 m/s) remains a persistent bottleneck for spaceborne Global Navigation Satellite System Reflectometry (GNSS-R). Conventional data-driven models often experience severe performance degradation in these regimes due to inherent physical limitations, including long-tail data distributions, low signal-to-noise ratios (SNR), and scattering signal saturation. To transcend these limitations, this study proposes the Physics-Guided Local-Global Fusion Network (PLGF-NET), establishing a novel physics-data dual-driven paradigm. At the data level, a Comprehensive Difficulty Score (CDS) is introduced to quantify the intrinsic physical complexity of Delay-Doppler Maps (DDMs). This metric drives a difficulty-aware hierarchical sampling strategy that rectifies long-tail biases and dynamically mines the scarce, high-wind scattering signatures. Within the network, a Physics-Guided Spatial Attention (PGSA) mechanism translates specular reflection theory into a structural inductive bias. This enforces a rigorous feature purification process, locking the receptive field onto the effective scattering window while suppressing peripheral thermal noise. Furthermore, geophysical consistency is guaranteed through a selective regularization mechanism governed by Sample Prediction Difficulty (SPD). Rather than applying uniform constraints, this approach adaptively enforces Geophysical Model Function (GMF) constraints exclusively on high-uncertainty samples, providing a robust physical anchor against signal saturation. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate the exceptional robustness of PLGF-NET. The framework achieves a state-of-the-art overall root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.38 m/s and drastically compresses the high-wind RMSE to 2.40 m/s, effectively correcting systematic negative biases. Ultimately, this scalable and physically interpretable architecture provides a highly reliable Earth observation tool for high-wind marine environment monitoring.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105493.title: PLGF-NET: A Physics-Guided Local-Global fusion network for GNSS-R high wind speed retrieval
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105493.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105495.abstract: Accurate mapping of perennial orchards is essential for agricultural management but remains challenging due to spatially discontinuous canopies and subtle phenological differences. This study presents an operational, application-oriented framework that integrates annual Very High-Resolution (VHR) aerial imagery (0.2 m) with monthly Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and Sentinel-2 optical time series to classify twelve orchard types across Israel from 2018 to 2023. By utilizing a multi-year dataset rather than a single seasonal cycle, we specifically evaluate model generalization and temporal robustness against inter-annual variability in phenology and imaging conditions. The dataset includes 106,413 labeled parcel-year samples from 19,950 parcels. We evaluate three model families: (i) satellite-only, (ii) VHR-only, and (iii) a multimodal mid-fusion deep-learning model (integrating spatial-structural and spectral-temporal modalities), under the same-year and cross-year (leave-one-year-out) scenarios. The satellite stream is modeled with a Lightweight Temporal Attention Encoder (LTAE) to capture seasonal dynamics, while the VHR stream uses a Swin Transformer backbone to extract hierarchical spatial features from 0.2 m imagery. The fused model achieved the highest performance across all settings (same-year OA = 0.890 ± 0.009; cross-year OA = 0.881 ± 0.014), outperforming both satellite-only (0.83) and VHR-only models (same-year OA = 0.846; cross-year OA = 0.795). In the best-performing fused cross-year scenario, class-wise F1-scores ranged from 0.71 for apple to 0.99 for banana. Fusion provided the largest gains in early-stage orchards (ages 1–3), where sparse canopy cover weakens spectral signals, but VHR imagery reveals planting geometry. Per-class analyses show that fusion benefits decrease with increasing mean NDVI, highlighting strong gains for sparse or deciduous orchards and minimal gains for dense evergreens. Overall, the results demonstrate that phenological time series and VHR spatial structure are highly complementary, enabling robust, operational orchard-type mapping and informing cost-aware workflows that selectively prioritize VHR acquisitions for young or low-NDVI orchards.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105495.title: Fusing very high-resolution aerial imagery with Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 time series improves multi-year orchard type classification
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105495.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105507.abstract: Keeping vector building databases current requires deciding which database operations should be applied, rather than merely detecting binary geometric differences. Minor discrepancies caused by acquisition noise, representation style, or cartographic generalization may trigger unnecessary updates when using hand-tuned geometric thresholds. We present V-BUILD, a hybrid decision framework that assigns each matched building unit one of four operations: addition, deletion, replacement, or preservation. Deterministic rules handle existential decisions, while a geometry-aware graph Transformer learns the more ambiguous morphological decisions between replacement and preservation directly in the vector domain. The model encodes 1:1 to m:n matching relationships via Unified Correspondence Graphs and uses Adaptive Multi-stream Fusion to integrate node-, edge-, and graph-level geometric descriptors. Experiments on Amsterdam TOP10NL, Hamburg LoD1, and Mercer County OSM data, together with a difficult Amsterdam subset, show that V-BUILD performs well in within-domain evaluations on both authoritative and crowdsourced vector data, while leave-one-domain-out analysis indicates that direct cross-source transfer remains challenging under strong domain shift. On Amsterdam, V-BUILD achieves the best Replacement F1 of 89.44 %; on Mercer, it obtains the best Macro F1 of 88.51 %, outperforming the strongest GNN baseline by 4.22 percentage points; and on the difficult Amsterdam subset, it achieves a 4.51-percentage-point higher Replacement F1 than the strongest GNN baseline, with the associated reduction in paired sample-level errors confirmed by a two-sided exact McNemar test. These results indicate that V-BUILD reduces dependence on manually tuned geometric decision thresholds and provides a practical decision module for incremental vector building database updating.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105507.title: V-BUILD: A graph Transformer-based decision framework for selective updating of vector building data
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105507.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105500.abstract: Satellite-derived vegetation indices are widely used in forest monitoring, yet their interpretation is complicated by the fact that canopy reflectance integrates both environmental stress signals and structural variation in stands. This challenge is particularly important across broad ecological gradients, where relationships between optical metrics and stand attributes may be spatially non-stationary. Here, we analysed NDVI–stand structure relationships in Scots pine-dominated forests across the whole of Poland using 30 m HLSS30 imagery, LiDAR-derived stand metrics, and a Geographic Gaussian Process Generalised Additive Model (GGP-GAM). The study focused on closed-canopy, undisturbed Scots pine stands and examined annual NDVI variation in 2016–2022 across eight forest natural regions in relation to stand age, stand volume, top height, and the Relative Spacing Index (RSI). Mean NDVI showed persistent regional differentiation across Poland and ranged from 0.64 to 0.84. The proportion of NDVI variability explained by stand characteristics varied markedly among years and forest natural regions, indicating strong spatial and temporal heterogeneity in NDVI–structure relationships. In general, structural predictors explained a larger share of NDVI variation in years with more favourable moisture conditions, whereas in drought years this structural signal was less apparent, partly coinciding with lower and more compressed NDVI distributions. An illustrative regional analysis further showed that the direction and magnitude of the partial effects of stand attributes changed among years, demonstrating that the structural meaning of NDVI was not constant through time. The results show that NDVI should not be interpreted as a spatially invariant proxy of stand structure across heterogeneous forest landscapes. Instead, its information content depends on both regional context and annual moisture conditions. By combining harmonized optical time series, LiDAR-derived stand descriptors and spatially varying modelling, this study provides a framework for more robust interpretation of canopy greenness in large-area forest monitoring.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105500.title: Spatially varying NDVI–stand structure relationships in Scots pine forests across Poland using HLS, LiDAR metrics and GGP-GAM
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105500.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105486.abstract: Accurate plant disease detection remains challenging when using single-modality data, which fails to capture comprehensive disease-related features. However, many existing studies rely on pixel-level classification or prior plant segmentation and lack explicit modeling of cross-modal interactions, limiting their ability to distinguish between healthy and diseased plants. This study presents a spatial–spectral fusion deep learning framework (S2-PDD) that fuses uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAV)-based RGB imagery and hyperspectral-derived feature representations for plant-level detection of potato diseases (blackleg and Potato virus Y (PVY)), employing early fusion (modalities combined at the input stage) and middle fusion (features integrated at intermediate stages within the model backbone) strategies. The multimodal fusion models were compared against single-modal models and an existing S2ADet model. Model performance, assessed through five-fold cross-validation, demonstrated that multimodal models integrating RGB and vegetation index features achieved the highest mAPs of 86.65 ± 1.71 (%; E-RV model) and 85.74 ± 1.96 (M-RV), respectively. These mAPs were higher than those of all single-modal models, including the RGB-only (83.21 ± 1.46) and hyperspectral-only models (PCA features: 79.71 ± 1.45; vegetation index features: 85.31 ± 2.36). They also exceeded mAPs of multimodal models combining RGB with PCA features (early fusion: 83.00 ± 2.81; middle fusion: 83.11 ± 2.46; S2ADet: 84.04 ± 2.73), regardless of the fusion strategy. The superior performance highlights that vegetation index features provide strong class separability compared to other hyperspectral representations. The proposed models achieved strong plant-level detection performance, with AP of 78.65 ± 4.14 (E-RV) and 77.40 ± 3.46 (M-RV) for blackleg disease, as well as 84.82 ± 3.59 (E-RV) and 83.28 ± 3.86 (M-RV) for PVY. These results demonstrate the potential of UAV-based multimodal sensing for disease monitoring in cropping systems. A potato plant disease detection dataset was constructed and made publicly available, containing paired RGB and hyperspectral image tiles with bounding box annotations. The code is available at https://github.com/Tim-Agro/S2-PDD.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105486.title: Deep spatial-spectral fusion of UAV RGB and hyperspectral imagery for potato plant disease detection

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105512.abstract: Global cloud-top phase monitoring is constrained by an observing gap: passive imagers provide broad coverage but limited vertical phase information, whereas active sensors provide stronger physical constraints only along narrow tracks. Here we develop MAPLE-CP, a Multi-Angle Polarimetric Latent-Enhancement framework for FY-3G PMAI cloud-top phase retrieval. MAPLE-CP links shortwave-infrared multi-angle polarimetric scattering information, DQ-1 ACDL cloud-top lidar labels, physics-guided feature screening, compact latent augmentation, and independent lidar validation. From approximately 140 PMAI variables, 50 physically interpretable predictors were selected and enhanced with six self-supervised latent descriptors. Using a 142,362-sample PMAI–ACDL cloud-top phase corpus, MAPLE-CP achieved internal accuracy, macro-F1, and AUC of 0.946, 0.897, and 0.991, respectively, on the original internal test split. Grouped split diagnostics clarified the evidence boundary of this internal benchmark, and independent validation using 6,433 ground-based lidar samples from 31 Chinese sites gave an agreement of 0.788 and macro-F1 of 0.780 within this external network. On an availability-limited shared-collocation subset with MODIS, Himawari-9, and ground-based lidar, MAPLE-CP showed higher agreement and macro-F1, suggesting complementary PMAI polarimetric phase information rather than a global product ranking. Overall, MAPLE-CP supports scalable cloud-top phase mapping and exposes residual mixed-phase uncertainty.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105512.title: Global cloud phase monitoring from FY-3G multi-angle polarimetric observations using the new MAPLE-CP framework with independent multi-site lidar validation
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105512.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105523.abstract: Full-spectrum solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF; 650–800 nm) provides a powerful means to characterize vegetation functional status. However, current retrieval methods still exhibit substantial uncertainties due to their reliance on fixed spectral-shape assumptions or strong priors for SIF and reflectance reconstruction, introducing inherent model-form biases when these assumptions mismatch observations. To address this limitation, we propose a physics-constrained neural network, FSIF-PCNN, for flexible and robust full-spectrum SIF reconstruction. FSIF-PCNN leverages a U-Net architecture to extract multi-scale spectral features, while enforcing physical plausibility through radiative-transfer consistency constraints and spectral smoothness regularization. The method was evaluated using simulated test datasets and independent tower-based measurements through comparison with two existing methods (FSIF-iPCA and SIFFI). On the simulated test datasets, FSIF-PCNN achieved minimal systematic bias (ARE = -0.034 %) and superior spectral reconstruction accuracy (RMSE = 0.011 mW m−2 nm−1 sr-1; mean RRMSE = 3.87 %), outperforming FSIF-iPCA (mean RRMSE = 13.70 %) and SIFFI (mean RRMSE = 11.98 %). Tower-based validations confirmed exceptional agreement with SFM retrievals in the O2-A and O2-B bands (site-specific R2 > 0.95). Compared with FSIF-iPCA and SIFFI, FSIF-PCNN demonstrated stronger accuracy and robustness across all validation sites, achieving site-mean RRMSE values of 5.74 % (DM), 4.46 % (GC), and 9.62 % (XTS) in the O2-A band, and 14.64 % (DM), 6.85 % (GC), and 11.22 % (XTS) in the O2-B band. These results demonstrate that FSIF-PCNN provides a flexible and physically constrained framework for full-spectrum SIF reconstruction, achieving improved agreement with independent references at the validated red and far-red bands.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105523.title: FSIF-PCNN: A physics-constrained neural network for full-spectrum solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence reconstruction
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105523.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105537.abstract: Tree height is a key descriptor of forest canopy structure, yet a single nadir view captures only part of the directional structural information contained in canopy reflectance. This study investigated whether viewing geometry provides directional information useful for UAV-based optical tree-height retrieval in a Larix principis-rupprechtii plantation. Multi-angular reflectance observations extracted from overlapping UAV multispectral images were used to fit the RossThick–LiSparseR (RTLSR) kernel-driven bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) model. The fitted model was then used to reconstruct directional reflectance at 27 prescribed viewing geometries along the solar principal plane, while UAV-LiDAR data provided grid-level reference tree heights. Nine vegetation indices were derived and evaluated using linear regression, random forest, and gradient boosting regressor under single- and multi-angle schemes. DVI, EVI, GDVI, TVI, and GOSAVI exhibited consistent angle-dependent sensitivity to tree height, with their strongest correlations and lowest retrieval errors generally occurring within the intermediate forward-viewing sector (30°–45°) in the BRDF-derived dataset. For example, the absolute correlation between GDVI and tree height increased from 0.429 at nadir to 0.507 at 40°. Among the tested index–scheme–model combinations, the lowest validation error was obtained using GDVI under the Forward + 0° scheme with random forest, reducing RMSE from 2.19 m at nadir to 1.79 m (RMSE% = 10.25 %). However, the relative performance of the tested angular schemes varied among models, indicating that angular configuration and retrieval algorithm jointly affected performance, while increasing the number of angular features alone did not consistently reduce retrieval error. Overall, the findings indicate that viewing geometry can provide useful directional information for within-site optical tree-height retrieval and that intermediate forward-viewing information may complement nadir observations.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105537.title: Viewing-geometry effects on UAV-based tree height retrieval using BRDF-derived vegetation indices
