10.1016/j.jag.2026.105534.abstract: Multimodal change detection combines multi-source remote sensing data, such as optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images, to overcome the inherent limitations of single-mode imaging mechanisms, thereby enhancing the robustness and timeliness of change information updates. However, previous Optical-SAR change detection methods still face challenges, including inadequate modeling of both modality-invariant and modality-specific characteristics, difficulty in capturing cross-modal spatio-temporal dependencies, and underutilization of land cover structural context. To address these issues, we propose a novel Optical-SAR change detection framework, namely FSTS-Net. It combines semantic features from the frequency, spatial, and temporal domains with structural features to comprehensively capture change. First, we design a frequency-spatio-temporal feature encoder integrating wavelet convolution and graph optimization theory into a state-space model to decouple cross-modal features and model bi-temporal dependencies. Second, a multi-scale graph convolutional network is built to explicitly model the spatial correlations among surface objects, thereby enhancing the representation of structural features. Finally, an adaptive fusion strategy dynamically adjusts the contribution weights of semantic and structural features to adapt to changes in information, effectively enhancing genuine change signals while suppressing pseudo-change. Our method demonstrates superior generalization and robustness over existing multimodal change detection (MMCD) methods, achieving mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 67.81 % on BRIGHT, 64.84 % on Wuhan-Het, and 88.55 % on Delta-SN6 datasets. The proposed FSTS-Net provides a reliable solution for multimodal change analysis. The code will be made available at: https://github.com/liuxuanguang/FSTS-Net.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105534.title: Joint learning of frequency-spatio-temporal dependencies and structural context for optical-SAR change detection
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105534.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105539.abstract: Accurate mapping and monitoring of forest structure and composition in complex mountainous regions remain challenging because of crown occlusion, crown adhesion, and pronounced topographic variation. Moreover, current monitoring methods often focus on single-attribute retrieval and lack an integrated framework for collaborative multidimensional attribute extraction. To address these challenges, this study proposes a multi-task collaborative method for individual tree segmentation and integrated multidimensional attribute extraction in mountainous forests using deep learning and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) RGB imagery. A two-stage segmentation method combining a U-Net++ deep learning model with a marker-controlled watershed algorithm was developed, followed by a sequential transfer learning strategy to facilitate knowledge transfer among individual tree segmentation, tree height prediction, and forest type classification. The proposed method was evaluated over a 5 km × 5 km area within the Wanglang National Nature Reserve (WNNR) using manually delineated tree crowns and canopy height models (CHM) derived from UAV LiDAR data. The results showed that the two-stage segmentation method combined the semantic representation capability of deep learning with the geometric partitioning ability of the watershed algorithm, thereby reducing under-segmentation caused by crown occlusion and adhesion in mountainous forests. The omission rate decreased from 9.12 % to 4.67 %, while the F1-score increased from 0.9298 to 0.9537. Sequential transfer learning also improved individual-tree attribute prediction, with the RMSE of tree height prediction decreasing from 7.1504 m to 3.4825 m and the overall accuracy of forest type classification increasing from 81.68 % to 92.51 %. The proposed method enables integrated mapping of individual-tree location, crown width, tree height, and forest type in complex mountainous forests, providing detailed information for precision forest management and forest carbon assessment.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105539.title: A multi-task collaborative method for individual tree segmentation and multi-dimensional attribute extraction in mountainous areas using deep learning technologies
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105539.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105547.abstract: Hyperspectral and multispectral image fusion (HMIF) aims to reconstruct high spatial resolution hyperspectral images by jointly leveraging the complementary spectral information from hyperspectral imagery and the spatial details from high spatial resolution multispectral imagery. Existing deep learning-based methods typically improve fusion performance by enlarging the receptive field to capture richer spatial–spectral contextual information, which inevitably increase computational complexity and may introduce redundant spatial–spectral interactions. To address these issues, this study proposes a new multiscale Spatial-Conditioned Spectral Routing Network (SCSRNet). Specifically, a Dynamic Fusion Gate (DFG) module is first developed to adaptively regulate the contributions of hyperspectral and multispectral features based on local spatial characteristics. Subsequently, a Large-Kernel Spatial–Spectral Residual Block (LK-SSRB) is designed, in which a Multi-Scale Spatial Perception Module (MSPM) captures spatial contextual information with large receptive fields, while a Spatial-Conditioned Spectral Routing Module (SCSRM) is innovatively designed to dynamically establish spectral dependencies guided by spatial priors. Additionally, a Residual Scaling Connection (RSC) is introduced to improve optimization stability and feature propagation efficiency. Extensive experiments conducted on three public datasets (i.e. Pavia Center, Chikusei, and MDAS) and a self-collected UAV-based Daxing dataset have demonstrated that the proposed method consistently outperforms seven state-of-the-art approaches in both quantitative metrics and visual quality. The performance gains of the proposed SCSRNet observed on the MDAS dataset achieves improvements of 6.0%, 9.8%, 0.7%, 9.7%, and 7.2% over the second-best comparative method. Furthermore, SCSRNet achieves superior reconstruction performance with relatively low computational complexity, underscoring its effectiveness and practicality for HMIF.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105547.title: A multi-scale spatial-conditioned spectral routing network for hyperspectral and multispectral image fusion
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105547.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105546.abstract: Geostationary satellite-based PM2.5 mapping increasingly relies on data-driven models using top-of-atmosphere (TOA) reflectance. However, most existing approaches train a single estimator on temporally aggregated samples, implicitly assuming a stationary relationship between TOA radiative signals and near-surface PM2.5. This assumption overlooks the pronounced diurnal variability captured by geostationary satellites and limits the representation of hour-dependent aerosol–radiation interactions. To address this limitation, we developed a physically constrained multi-task learning framework, termed the Multi-Temporal Decoupled Attention Network (MTDAN), for hourly PM2.5 estimation from geostationary satellite TOA reflectance. The framework integrates three components: (1) a physically guided surface–atmosphere decoupling module that suppresses surface-background interference and enhances aerosol-sensitive information; (2) a multi-task attention architecture that jointly learns shared and hour-specific relationships between PM2.5 and explanatory variables; and (3) a temporal-constrained loss function that exploits diurnal continuity to improve the consistency of sequential predictions. Experiments over eastern China using year-long Himawari-8 observations and ground-based PM2.5 measurements demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed framework. MTDAN achieved an overall site-based validation R2 of 0.89 with an RMSE of 9.27 μg m⁻3, outperforming representative machine-learning and deep-learning models by reducing estimation errors by 21.7 %–27.8 %. The model successfully reproduced hourly pollution evolution, captured localized hotspots, and reconstructed season-dependent diurnal PM2.5 dynamics. Ablation analyses further confirmed the complementary contributions of physical decoupling, adaptive feature weighting, and temporal-consistency constraints. These results demonstrate that explicitly modeling hour-dependent aerosol–radiation relationships can substantially improve geostationary satellite-based PM2.5 estimation. The proposed framework provides an interpretable and robust solution for high-frequency air-quality monitoring and offers a general strategy for integrating physical constraints and temporal context into Earth observation applications.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105546.title: Improving hourly PM2.5 estimation from geostationary satellite TOA reflectance through physically constrained multi-task learning
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105546.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105553.abstract: Spatially continuous three-dimensional tropospheric delay fields are essential for Earth observation and atmospheric sensing. The ERA5 reanalysis offers continuous coverage but is delayed by several days, whereas Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) observations are accurate and near-real-time but pointwise. This study develops Tropoformer-S, an iTransformer-based framework that reconstructs the regional delay field by integrating the two sources. The framework forecasts the ERA5-derived level-wise Zenith Tropospheric Delay (ZTD) at 15 pressure levels from 1000 to 550 hPa for 1 to 120 h, where the variate-token attention explicitly models the spatial correlation among grid points. The forecast field is converted into station ZTD through a physically guided retrieval chain and refined by GNSS-informed corrections along two complementary paths, harmonic self-correction for stations with local GNSS records and spatial reconstruction of the bias field for stations without. Over mainland China, the forecasts attain a level-mean RMSE of 2.84 cm against the ERA5-derived ZTD and outperform five alternative deep-learning architectures. The overall RMSE is 3.20 cm in 2022 and 3.23 cm in 2023 against GNSS, on average 18.64 % and 33.10 % below GPT3 and HGPT2, and the radiosonde evaluation shows a near-zero bias. The harmonic correction path lowers the RMSE to 2.79 and 2.98 cm and reduces the network bias to near zero, while the spatial correction path reaches 2.10 to 2.66 cm at withheld stations under nine network densities and largely removes the lead dependence. The framework thus fills the ERA5 latency gap with continuous tropospheric delay information for geodetic and atmospheric applications.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105553.title: Tropoformer-S: iTransformer-based spatiotemporal reconstruction of three-dimensional tropospheric delay fields integrating ERA5 reanalysis and GNSS observations
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105553.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105561.abstract: As a virtual component of the geospatial digital twin (GDT), the virtual geographic environment (VGE) has significant advantages in enhancing human geographic cognition and analyzing and solving practical engineering problems. However, existing virtual geographic scene modeling methods still have significant gaps compared to GDT, making it difficult to balance the ability to represent dynamic objects as required by GDT while preserving the geographic characteristics of VGE, such as spatiotemporal reference and multiscale representation. Against this backdrop, this paper takes highway tunnel scenes as an example. It proposes a modeling framework that leverages the synergy between perception data and scene knowledge to construct a virtual geographic scene for GDT. First, we constructed a multi-domain integrated knowledge graph of highway tunnel scenes to enhance the standardization and completeness of the modeling process. Second, we established a dynamic object detection network based on an improved YOLOv8 model, endowing the virtual geographic scene with the capability to represent dynamic objects. Third, we proposed a tunnel scene twin modeling method that integrates a knowledge graph with a perception network, enabling effective fusion of the static base and dynamic objects. Finally, we selected a tunnel in China as the study area, developed a prototype system, and conducted experimental analyses. The results demonstrate that the proposed method successfully constructs a GDT-oriented virtual geographic scene for highway tunnels. For the city-level model, over 93.6 % of points have an error of less than 0.1 m; for the component-level model, over 95.4 % of points have an error of less than 0.01 m; the model’s semantic accuracy reaches 95 %; the average modeling time for dynamic targets is 11.8 ms; and the average rendering efficiency of the virtual scene is 133.2 FPS. Furthermore, compared to existing scene modeling methods, the constructed scene integrates advantages such as geospatial and temporal references, multiscale representation, and dynamic object representation. Research results provide an example reference for intelligent management of urban traffic, and provide new ideas for virtual geographical scene modeling.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105561.title: Virtual geographical scene modeling towards geospatial digital twins: A case study of urban highway tunnel scenarios
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105561.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105567.abstract: Selective logging (SL) is a major driver of forest degradation, yet its small and short-lived canopy openings remain difficult to detect in persistently cloudy tropical regions. Optical approaches miss many events, while synthetic aperture radar (SAR) time series are challenging to model with architectures that either fuse multivariate features too early or smooth over transient signals. We present InterFormer, a Transformer-based architecture that jointly models feature interactions and temporal dynamics via a feature block with Multi-head Intercross Self Attention (MISA) and a temporal block with Multi-head Self Dissimilar Attention (MSDA). Texture features were further utilized as complementary input. Since precise SL labels are unavailable, the model was trained and internally tested using a weak-label benchmark, in which pixel labels were extracted within the official published Real-Time Deforestation Detection System (DETER) polygons. To complement this internal weak-label benchmark, we designed two independent practical experiments to evaluate the model performance in low-intensity Annual Production Units (UPAs) based on field-inventory data and at the municipality scale (> 30,000 km2) in the Brazilian Amazon. In the independent UPA validation, InterFormer localized 92.65% of tree-falling gaps in UPA areas and outperformed standard Transformer variants and Planet-based alerts from the Brazilian Forest Service by approximately 20% at the tree level. At the municipality level, our predicted alert polygons achieved the highest Detection Rate against DETER across multiple reference-overlap thresholds in both Paragominas and Feliz Natal, while also producing fewer unmatched alerts than RAdar for Detecting Deforestation (RADD) and Tropical Moist Forest dataset (TMF). However, substantial over-expansion of predicted alert regions remained. These results suggest that InterFormer provides a useful framework for representing weak and short-lived SL signals in Sentinel-1 time series, and that openly available SAR data have the potential to support large-scale SL monitoring under weak supervision. Nevertheless, the current municipality-scale workflow still relies on optical-derived masking as a supporting step, and the development of a fully SAR-only large-area monitoring framework remains an important direction for future work.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105567.title: Mapping selective logging with Sentinel-1 image time series and a novel transformer-based model
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105567.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105525.abstract: Hyperspectral and LiDAR images, as a class of multi-source remote sensing data, have their own advantageous features. HSI contains rich spectral information, compared to LiDAR, which is more capable of reflecting the height information of the target area. However, determining the intrinsic correlation characteristics between HSI channels and fully exploiting the complementary characteristics of HSI and LiDAR to improve classification accuracy remains a challenging issue. In this paper, we propose a graph-interactive collaborative learning network (GICL-Net) for joint classification of HSI and LiDAR, which consists of a multi-scale spectral-spatial graph feature extractor (MSGE) and a cross-modality adjacency matrix fusion (CAMF) module. Specifically, MSGE is divided into two branches. One branch starts from the spectral dimension, defining each channel of HSI as a node to construct a graph network and mine potential correlations at the channel level, thereby capturing the intrinsic spectral correlation features of the target region. The other branch focuses on the height information of the target area, constructing a graph network at the geometric spatial level to extract representative height features. The CAMF module leverages the fused adjacency matrix to establish a cross-modal graph interaction mechanism, enabling the spectral features and the spatial features to achieve deep synergy through iterative updates in graph convolution. This generates cross-modal fusion features with fine spectral discrimination capability and spatial dimensional structural integrity. This method has been validated for effectiveness across multiple HSI and LiDAR datasets. In particular, on the Houston2013 dataset, the overall accuracy (OA) reached 98.91%, with a Kappa coefficient of 0.9882. Furthermore, compared with the baseline network (i.e., the conventional two-branch graph network, the overall accuracy improved by 6.58%. Our code is available at the link: https://github.com/Xidian-AIGroup190726/GICLNet.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105525.title: GICL-Net: A graph-interactive collaborative learning network for joint classification of HSI and LiDAR
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105525.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105568.abstract: To address the issues of insufficient resolution and a lack of fine-grained categories in traditional land use and land cover (LULC) products, this study integrates lightweight deep learning, a decoder-centric multi-task learning architecture, and a significant change attention mechanism to propose a deep learning framework (Decoder-Centric Attention Network, DecAttNet) for large-scale, high-precision land use change mapping. By mitigating cross‑task feature conflicts within the multitask‑learning framework via its significant‑change attention module, DecAttNet can adaptively focus on key change areas while sharing features and improving computational efficiency. Additionally, this study utilized DecAttNet to generate a 2023 land‑use product for North China (ten provinces, municipalities and autonomous regions) (LULC_NorthChina_2023) comprising 28 fine‑grained land‑cover classes based on 2‑meter high‑resolution imagery. The results of this study demonstrate that (1) DecAttNet significantly outperforms other deep learning models in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency, with an average overall accuracy of 90.28 %, which is higher than the figures achieved by the FCNN model (83.12 %), the ChangeMask model (87.73 %), the BGSNet model (86.63 %), and the TripleS model (88.24 %), while improving computational efficiency by approximately 44 % compared to the FCNN model. (2) Based on an independent field validation dataset, the DecAttNet model achieved high extraction precision (precision = 94.86 %) for changed land cover features. (3) The LULC_NorthChina_2023 dataset constructed in this study, which is based on the DecAttNet model, combines high precision (precision = 91.85 %) with high spatial detail. (4) The DecAttNet model demonstrates significant temporal generalization capabilities, achieving average classification accuracies of 89.23 % and 88.78 % in selected sample test regions in 2024 and 2025, respectively, with interannual variability of less than 1.5 %, and exhibits high stability across different geographic re. The DecAttNet framework provides an efficient and accurate solution for large-scale, high-resolution land use dynamic monitoring, and the resulting dataset serves as a valuable benchmark for fine-scale environmental research.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105568.title: DecAttNet: A decoder-centric multi-task attention network for rapid, large-scale land use change detection and 2 M resolution products generation
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105568.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105595.abstract: Continuous, high-frequency observations of aerosol optical depth (AOD) are crucial for understanding aerosol dynamics and regional air quality. However, individual geostationary (GEO) AOD products suffer from distinct spatiotemporal gaps and uncertainties driven by cloud screening, surface-reflectance assumptions, and strict algorithmic quality controls. To address these limitations, we propose a deep-learning fusion framework synergizing the spectral, temporal, and geometric complementarities of three GEO satellites (GK-2B, Himawari-9, and FY-4B) over East Asia. Central to our framework is a TabNet-based dynamic feature selection mechanism that adaptively weights heterogeneous multi-sensor inputs to suppress local retrieval errors. To improve spatial generalization, we implement a two-stage transfer learning strategy: pre-training with spatially extensive MODIS data to establish large-scale spatial priors, followed by fine-tuning with ground-based AERONET observations. Compared to single-satellite baselines, the fused AOD product from May 2024 to April 2025 improves accuracy and spatiotemporal coverage. Specifically, it yields an overall cross-validation correlation coefficient (R) of 0.94, reduces root-mean-square error (RMSE) by 47 %, and increases valid hourly matchups by 33.5 %. Independent-site validation shows consistent generalizability (R = 0.88). Furthermore, evaluations of extreme events, including severe biomass-burning and dust transport episodes, demonstrate that the fused AOD product can reconstruct hourly plume gradients during rapid transport. By improving the temporal characterization of complex aerosol environments, this deep learning-driven fusion approach provides a useful foundational dataset for future regional air-quality analyses and chemical transport model assimilation.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105595.title: Tracking diurnal aerosol dynamics and smoke transport over East Asia using multi-geostationary satellite fusion (GK-2B, Himawari-9, FY-4B)
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105595.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105569.abstract: The precise oriented detection of dense and small-scale ships within Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery constitutes a significant challenge for automated maritime surveillance systems because of intense clutter, minimal target sizes, and arbitrary rotations. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a coordinated multi-stage feature refinement framework, termed DiFE-TransOBB, tailored for dense SAR ship detection. Rather than relying on isolated module enhancements, the proposed architecture establishes a progressive interaction mechanism across structural, spatial, and frequency domains. Specifically, the Directional Feature Excavator (DiFE) module can extract geometry-aware structural priors to suppress isotropic clutter interference, the High-Resolution Spatial Fidelity Preservation Branch (HSFPB) preserves fine-grained localization details of tiny ships, and the Dual-Domain Interaction Fusion (DualFusion) performs conditional frequency-domain refinement guided by these spatial-structural cues to disentangle ship contours from unstructured high-frequency sea clutter. Evaluated on the newly constructed DenseSARShip-v1 benchmark and further validated on public datasets, DiFE-TransOBB achieved the highest detection performance among the evaluated methods while maintaining a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and cross-dataset generalization capability of the proposed framework for oriented ship detection in dense and cluttered SAR scenes.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105569.title: A directional feature excavation transformer for oriented detection of small-scale ships in dense SAR imagery
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105569.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105575.abstract: Early-season forest decline in temperate broadleaved stands often lacks detectable biochemical stress signals, manifesting primarily through reduced foliage density and increased visibility of non-photosynthetic vegetation (NPV). This study investigated the spectral separability of green leaves and NPV components under varying levels of canopy defoliation. Using a crane platform, we collected in situ leaf- and canopy-level spectrometer measurements alongside co-aligned photography to quantify the visible fraction of NPV. We analyzed the multi-angular reflectance characteristics and evaluated 35 vegetation indices (VIs) —including green biomass metrics and specialized NPV indices —using Random Forest to identify optimal spectral and geometric configurations. Sunlit young foliage exhibited high forward scatter, creating a nadir reflectance minimum. At canopy level, a nadir minimum was driven by the gap distribution resulting from sustainable forest management practices. Consequently, the optimal viewing angle for top-ranking VIs (e.g., SNCBAO, Ctr2, mNDVI705) was near the hotspot geometry, minimizing shadowing and forest floor interference. While the total visible fraction of NPV remained mostly insensitive to viewing angles, its shaded proportion varied. VIs targeting green vegetation via red-edge and NIR domains consistently outperformed dedicated NPV indices based on SWIR cellulose and lignin absorption. This is attributed to low upper-canopy SWIR transmittance, which obscured the signals of the largely shaded NPV fraction. Top-performing VIs achieved R2 = 0.92 for NPV visibility prediction, improving by 21 % over the best SWIR indices and 11 % over the nadir view. To accurately detect initial defoliation and overcome forest floor interference, adopting off-nadir viewing geometries is advantageous for capturing the optimal signal.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105575.title: Multi-angular assessment of early-season defoliation: Evaluating the sensitivity of vegetation indices to NPV visibility in temperate broadleaved forests
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105575.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105583.abstract: Parametric models are foundational to Building Information Modeling (BIM) and digital construction, enabling efficient design, analysis, and lifecycle management. However, most 3D building models reconstructed from real-world data sources — such as 3D scanning, photogrammetry, or format conversion — are represented as unstructured mesh models. Although these meshes accurately capture geometric shape, they typically lack the parametric constraints, design intent, and procedural history inherent to native BIM objects. This semantic deficiency severely limits their direct applicability in workflows that require model editing, parametric adjustment, or semantic interpretation. To address this challenge, this paper presents an automated framework for semantic lifting of unstructured architectural mesh models into structured, procedural parametric CAD models. The proposed pipeline first analyzes the geometric and topological characteristics of the input mesh and employs a deep learning-based module to predict a plausible sequence of CAD modeling operations. Subsequently, a 2D parametric profile abstraction and parameterization module processes the geometric regions involved in the predicted operations, transforming them into constrained and editable 2D parametric profiles composed of basic geometric primitives, such as lines, arcs, and circles. Finally, a parameterization-driven reconstruction module executes the recovered operation sequence and parametric planar profiles within a CAD environment to procedurally regenerate a structured solid model with full parametric editability. Extensive experiments on diverse architectural datasets demonstrate the robustness of the proposed approach, showing that it can generate parametric CAD models that closely match the original mesh geometry while supporting reliable parameter-driven editing. This research provides an effective pathway for the semantic lifting of mesh-based building models, enabling their reuse in BIM reconstruction, digital twins, and architectural analysis applications.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105583.title: Automated conversion of unstructured mesh models to structured parametric CAD models for architectural applications

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105594.abstract: Railway-corridor deformation monitoring requires timely identification of localized displacement anomalies and characterization of their temporal evolution. Time-series Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) provides spatially dense and high-precision displacement observations from repeated SAR acquisitions, but InSAR-based railway studies have largely remained rate-centered, leaving the kinematic information embedded in displacement time series insufficiently exploited. This study develops a kinematic interpretation framework that integrates InSAR displacement time series, transfer learning-based Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) classification, and multi-source environmental data to characterize railway-corridor deformation in terms of its occurrence, temporal evolution, and environmental context. Sentinel-1 images acquired from January 2022 to December 2024 were processed to retrieve LOS displacement rates and displacement time series along the Kunming–Yuxi section of the China–Laos Railway. To reduce dependence on labeled InSAR samples, a transfer learning strategy was adopted, in which the TCN was pre-trained using simulated displacement sequences and fine-tuned with labeled InSAR observations to classify six kinematic patterns: stable, linear, step, piecewise linear, power-law, and undefined. The corridor is generally stable, with a mean displacement rate of −0.26 mm/year and stable points accounting for 77.96% of observations. Linear and step patterns account for 12.66% and 7.87%, respectively. Strong subsidence zones, where the localized displacement rate reaches −28.43 mm/year, are dominated by linear deformation. Pattern-based interpretation further shows that non-stable deformation is associated with Quaternary unconsolidated sediments, paddy soils, fine-grained soil textures, and urban expansion areas. These results indicate that InSAR-derived kinematic patterns provide an effective interpretive layer for linking railway-corridor displacement, temporal evolution, and environmental context.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105594.title: Kinematic pattern interpretation of railway-corridor deformation from InSAR time series with transfer learning-based TCN

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105625.abstract: Shrub encroachment can alter forage resources, soil–water processes, and landscape configuration in alpine grasslands, yet annual mapping remains challenging because shrub and herbaceous canopies converge spectrally and many apparent changes occur in diffuse ecotones. We developed a 10-m annual mapping framework integrating Sentinel-2 phenology, Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) time-series information, and topographic covariates to distinguish shrubland from grassland in Maqu County on the northeastern Tibetan Plateau from 2018 to 2024. A learned SAR-derived shrubland-grassland discrimination score (SGDS) was constructed from annual Sentinel-1 descriptors using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-regularized logistic regression to improve shrubland-grassland discrimination. In the 2024 benchmark experiment, the selected random forest (RF) configuration reduced classification error by approximately 17% relative to optical-only RF. SGDS outperformed the tested conventional SAR indices and the full SAR-statistics feature set, and adding SGDS increased RF accuracy from 91.26% to 92.47%. When the selected workflow was applied independently to each mapping year, annual overall accuracies ranged from 91.6% to 95.8%, based on the same 500 temporally screened reference locations spatially separated from the model-development samples. Nominal mapped shrubland area increased from 392.3 km2 in 2018 to 648.2 km2 in 2022 before declining to 560.4 km2 in 2024. Confidence and boundary-sensitivity analyses showed that the pronounced 2020–2021 increase was largely associated with low-confidence ecotonal pixels and decreased from + 96.91 to + 6.09 km2 as the mapped-class confidence threshold increased from 0.60 to 0.80, whereas the 2022–2024 decline remained negative under all tested confidence and boundary screens. Mapped shrubland area showed an apparent positive association with annual mean temperature, but this relationship was not robust after detrending and should be considered preliminary given the seven-year record. Overall, integrating learned SAR structural information with optical phenology improved annual shrubland-grassland mapping and provided a more reliable basis for interpreting mapped dynamics, with potential for locally calibrated application in comparable alpine regions.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105625.title: Fine-scale annual mapping and dynamic monitoring of shrub encroachment in alpine grasslands by integrating Sentinel-2 phenological features with Sentinel-1 structural information

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105588.abstract: Chlorophyll a (Chl-a) is widely used to indicate eutrophication and bloom risk in inland waters, but daily Sentinel-3 observations alone cannot resolve transient sub-daily variability represented in partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a records. This study therefore develops VGTA (Vision Mamba–GKOA–TCN-Attention), a staged remote-sensing-assisted and in situ-constrained framework that integrates daily Sentinel-3 OLCI-derived priors with partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a sequences and binary observation masks. A 20-dimensional OLCI-derived feature space provides spectral–spatial priors for Chl-a estimation and bloom-risk state identification. GKOA optimizes TCN-Attention to reconstruct masked values within partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a sequences. Vision Mamba outperformed CNN– and Transformer-based models in Chl-a estimation, achieving 94.8% accuracy, a Macro-F1 score of 0.909, and a Bloom-F1 score of 0.870. Ablation experiments confirmed the contributions of bidirectional contextual modeling, positional embedding, selective state-space modeling, and gating. Under Missing Completely at Random, block-missing, and real missing scenarios, GTA improved reconstruction performance by 12.71–55.54% relative to the best baseline models. Uncertainty increased once continuous gaps reached seven days, defining a practical boundary of data-driven reconstruction. Chl-a fluctuations and bloom-risk transitions can unfold within a day, and daily satellite snapshots may blur their timing or miss short events. Reconstruction of masked time steps within partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a sequences can support earlier identification of bloom-risk transitions, more timely field sampling and management responses, and temporally finer monitoring of inland waters.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105588.title: Remote-sensing-assisted and in situ-constrained reconstruction of 4-hourly chlorophyll-a dynamics in inland lakes using vision Mamba and temporal attention

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105611.abstract: Leaf Area Index (LAI) is a fundamental variable for characterizing vegetation canopy structure and ecosystem functioning. However, persistent cloud contamination substantially constrains the spatiotemporal continuity of LAI products derived from polar-orbiting satellite observations. In contrast, geostationary satellites provide dense temporal sampling, offering a valuable observational basis for filling data gaps in polar-orbiting satellite products. To bridge this observational gap, this study develops an observation-complementary framework that integrates high-frequency Himawari-8 Advanced Himawari Imager (AHI) observations with MODIS LAI products to achieve LAI reconstruction in cloud-prone regions. Within this framework, AHI observations are first used to retrieve LAI at a spatial resolution of 2 km using a Random Forest model trained with a high-quality MODIS-based benchmark dataset, and are then downscaled to 500 m using MODIS-derived spatial texture information. The reconstructed AHI LAI is subsequently integrated into low-quality or missing MODIS pixels to generate a fused AHI-MODIS LAI dataset over China. Validation against in-situ measurements and cross-comparison results show that the fused product maintains reasonable numerical consistency and stable temporal trajectories. Data availability increases from 70.70% to 90.90% under the 4-day compositing cycle. These results indicate that geostationary-polar-orbiting observation complementarity provides a practical pathway for improving the continuity and usability of optical LAI products in persistently cloudy regions, while remaining subject to the constraints of optical observations and cross-scale reconstruction assumptions.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105611.title: Bridging cloud-induced gaps in MODIS leaf area index products using high-frequency geostationary satellite observations
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105611.source: ScienceDirect official citation and abstract BibTeX export

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105616.abstract: Plant functional traits provide critical indicators of ecosystem functioning, biodiversity maintenance, and plant adaptive strategies under environmental change. However, hyperspectral retrieval of mangrove functional traits remains challenging because trait-related spectral signals are strongly influenced by species composition, canopy structural heterogeneity, and intertidal background effects, leading to unstable trait-spectrum relationships across species and scales. To address these limitations, this study developed a genetic algorithm-optimized extreme learning machine (GA-ELM) framework for robust retrieval of mangrove functional traits under heterogeneous mangrove spectral conditions. Three key traits, including chlorophyll content (Cab), equivalent water thickness (EWT), and leaf mass per area (LMA), were retrieved for four dominant mangrove species using leaf-level hyperspectral measurements and canopy-scale GF-5 imagery. GA-ELM generally outperformed PLSR, RF, and conventional ELM in species-specific comparisons. Leave-one-species-out validation yielded R2 ranges of 0.61–0.75 for Cab, 0.60–0.72 for EWT, and 0.66–0.76 for LMA, indicating moderate predictive capability for previously unseen species, with performance varying among species and traits. At the canopy scale, GA-ELM achieved stable estimation accuracy for Cab, EWT, and LMA based on GF-5 imagery (R2 > 0.75), demonstrating that the framework can be independently calibrated for canopy-scale retrieval. Independent cross-regional validation yielded R2 values of 0.60, 0.49, and 0.44 for Cab, EWT, and LMA, respectively, indicating moderate but reduced cross-regional transferability. Spectral sensitivity and band-selection analyses revealed species- and trait-dependent patterns that provided context for interpreting variation in predictive performance. These results remain conditional on one GF-5 acquisition per site and 30 m mixed-pixel conditions, and broader tidal-stage and cross-sensor validation is still required. These findings demonstrate the potential of GA-ELM for hyperspectral retrieval and spatial mapping of mangrove functional traits.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105616.title: Robust hyperspectral retrieval of mangrove functional traits across species and spatial scales using GA-ELM

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105639.abstract: Time-series Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) provides dense displacement observations along urban rail corridors, yet converting point-based measurements into corridor-scale diagnostic information remains challenging. This study proposes the Metro-InSAR Risk Index (MIRI), a diagnostic index designed to convert multi-dimensional InSAR-derived displacement characteristics into displacement-related diagnostic levels for urban metro corridors. MIRI integrates displacement rate, cumulative displacement, local displacement heterogeneity, height-related variability, and temporal residual variability, thereby extending conventional velocity-based interpretation toward corridor-scale displacement-risk diagnosis. The framework was applied to the Kunming Metro Network using 198 descending Sentinel-1 images acquired from March 2018 to December 2024. The time-series InSAR results show that the network was generally stable, with line-of-sight (LOS) displacement rates mainly ranging from −6 to 3 mm/yr and 97.21% of coherent scatterers falling within the stable interval of −3 to 3 mm/yr. Localized displacement anomalies were mainly observed near line intersections, curved sections, construction-affected areas, and the Dianchi Lake shoreline. Based on MIRI, 78%, 17%, 4%, and 1% of valid points were classified as Levels D, C, B, and A, respectively, indicating a distribution dominated by lower diagnostic levels, with spatially confined Level-B and Level-A anomalies particularly along Lines 4 and 5 and in lakeside soft-ground areas. Multi-source contextual variables and XGBoost-SHAP analysis were further used to interpret the environmental, anthropogenic, operational, and displacement-gradient information associated with the MIRI-based diagnostic patterns. The results indicate that the spatial variation in MIRI is mainly associated with terrain-related conditions, corridor-scale displacement variation, metro operation, and urban development intensity. By deriving diagnostic levels directly from PSI-based displacement indicators, MIRI provides an InSAR-based screening tool for prioritizing displacement-related anomalies and supporting maintenance of urban rail transit systems.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105639.title: A Metro-InSAR Risk Index for corridor-scale displacement risk diagnosis of urban rail infrastructure

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105641.abstract: Accurate retrieval of water-quality parameters from remote-sensing imagery is essential for monitoring large inland lakes, yet pronounced spatial heterogeneity and limited transferability across varying environmental conditions remain major challenges. This study proposes a Prior-Informed Spatially Adaptive Network (PISA-Net) for multi-parameter water-quality retrieval from Sentinel-2 imagery in Poyang Lake. PISA-Net integrates a CNN branch for nonlinear spectral–spatial feature learning with a knowledge-guided branch based on empirical optical descriptors and coordinate-derived geographic priors. A geographic soft-assignment mechanism constructs the spatial prior vector, which conditions CNN features through Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM), while a stop gradient consistency loss (SG-CL) promotes agreement between the two prediction pathways with controlled gradient propagation. Chl-a, TP, and CODMn were modeled independently and evaluated using 5-fold spatial-block cross-validation against six representative empirical, statistical, machine-learning, and deep-learning baselines. PISA-Net achieved R2 values of 0.6113, 0.5112, and 0.5054 for Chl-a, TP, and CODMn, respectively, consistently outperforming the strongest baseline, 2D-CNN, while reducing RMSE by approximately 29.6%, 21.4%, and 19.0%. An additional April 2018 cross-season experiment revealed substantial degradation under direct zero-shot transfer, whereas few-shot adaptation markedly reduced prediction errors, indicating useful cross-season adaptability after limited local calibration. Overall, PISA-Net provides a prior-informed spectral–spatial framework for water-quality retrieval under spatially heterogeneous conditions, while broader multi-season validation remains necessary to establish comprehensive seasonal generalizability.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105641.title: Prior-Informed Spatially Adaptive Network (PISA-Net) for multi-parameter water quality retrieval in Poyang Lake using Sentinel-2 imagery

10.1016/j.jag.2026.105652.abstract: Mountain vegetation dynamics serve as sensitive indicators of environmental change, making accurate fractional cover mapping of primary components crucial for understanding ecosystem responses. This task has been facilitated by multispectral satellite imagery, particularly Sentinel-2, which provides continuous observations. To translate these observations into fractional cover maps, existing studies typically apply fraction estimation models to synthetic spectra derived from field-measured signatures. However, limited field surveys in mountain terrain present a data bottleneck for synthetic spectra construction, while complex vegetation composition introduces spectral ambiguities that existing methods struggle to represent. Therefore, this study develops a knowledge-guided unmixing framework for annual mapping of the fractional cover of herbaceous vegetation, woody vegetation, and bare land in mountain environments using Sentinel-2 time series. Specifically, to overcome data bottleneck, we develop a knowledge-guided strategy that automatically builds adaptive physio-phenological feature spaces to extract representative signatures. To resolve spectral ambiguity, we incorporate nonlinear mixing mechanisms to synthesize spectra that better represent complex mixing relationships. The synthetic library was then used to train Unmix-Net, a spectral-temporal regression model for fraction estimation. The framework was applied to the central Qilian Mountains and southern Hengduan Mountains spanning broad climatic gradients, validated with high-resolution UAV data. It achieved MAEs of 12.38 %, 8.58 %, and 9.82 % for herbaceous, woody, and bare land, outperforming existing models by up to 7.80 %. When implemented across landscapes ranging from arid steppes and alpine meadows to tropical rainforests, the framework maintained comparable performance. The comparative experiments further confirmed that the proposed extraction strategy improved the balance of component estimates, while combining complementary mixing mechanisms reduced estimation errors. By integrating domain knowledge into data-driven learning, this framework supports spatially continuous fractional vegetation mapping in mountain environments.
10.1016/j.jag.2026.105652.title: Towards fractional vegetation cover mapping in complex mountain environments through a knowledge-guided unmixing framework
